name: SE_ArrayCopy
semantics: Copies src[srcStart .. end) into dst starting at dstStart. NOTE: 5th argument is an END INDEX in src, not a length. srcSize=ArraySize(src) (0 if not an array), dstSize=ArraySize(dst). If end<0 or end>srcSize then end=srcSize. Loop: while dstIdx<dstSize and srcIdx<end: dst[dstIdx]=copy of src[srcIdx] (ArraySetElement/CopyCell: reference types share the object, refcount+1); srcIdx++, dstIdx++. Loop is skipped entirely if dstStart>=dstSize. Out-of-range srcIdx (negative srcStart) gives NULL element -> CopyCell(NULL) stores int 0; negative dstIdx writes are silently ignored (ArraySetElement returns 0) while indexes keep advancing. Non-array dst or src: size 0 -> nothing copied. Always returns int 0.
notes: Native frame: handler reads args[k] (cell at args+5k, value dword at +1) WITHOUT checking argc unless stated, so a missing argument reads a stale stack cell. Dispatcher always returns 1 (never aborts the step). Arg layout from dis: dstStart=[args+6], srcStart=[args+0x10], end=[args+0x15]. Source and destination may be the same array (forward copy, overlapping not handled specially).

name: SE_TableClone
semantics: Returns a NEW table (SetCellNewTable on the task result: 4 buckets, auto-key counter=1, fresh id) filled by walking t in its iteration order (TableNextEntry from NULL) and inserting each (key,value copy) with TableInsertAndGrow (append at chain tail, rehash x2 when count>=4*buckets). If the argument is not a table (or empty) returns an empty new table. Values are copied with CopyCell (nested arrays/tables/strings shared by reference, not deep-cloned). The auto-key counter of the clone is NOT copied (restarts at 1). Iteration order of the clone can differ from the source (insertion history differs, rehash reverses chains).
notes: Result is written straight into task->result then ResumeTask. Hash/iteration details: bucket index = int key & (n-1); string key h=c+2*h over bytes then &(n-1); other key types bucket 0 (TableSet never matches them, so duplicates are appended). TableSet appends new nodes at the TAIL of the chain; TableRehash relinks every node at the HEAD of its new chain (walking old buckets 0..n-1, old chain order), so chains get reversed on each rehash. Iteration = buckets ascending, chain order. Grow condition after insert: count > 4*buckets-1.

name: SE_StringSplit
semantics: Splits s on every non-overlapping occurrence of sep (strstr, case-sensitive; scan restarts at match+len(sep)). Returns array of count+1 heap strings: pieces before each separator, then the remainder (so trailing separator gives a trailing empty string; empty s gives [""]; no match gives [s]). Separator pieces are not included. Empty sep: strstr(s,"") returns s every time -> the counting loop never ends (hang). Non-string s or sep: CellGetString returns NULL -> access violation (crash). Result via ResumeTaskWithCell (array copy).
notes: strstr is Crt::Strstr 0x005108e0 (plain CRT). Pieces created with SetCellStringDup(ptr,len), last with ArraySetString.

name: SE_ArrayInsert
semantics: Inserts a copy of value (CopyCell) at position index, shifting later elements up; size+1. index<0 means append; index>size silently fails (nothing changes); index==size appends. If arr is not an array (or null) nothing happens. Always returns int 0 (the -1 from ArrayInsert is discarded). Capacity grows by 8 cells when full. Empty/lazy arrays are handled as normal arrays.
notes: Native frame: handler reads args[k] (cell at args+5k, value dword at +1) WITHOUT checking argc unless stated, so a missing argument reads a stale stack cell. Dispatcher always returns 1 (never aborts the step). Calls ArrayInsert(index=args[1].value, array=args[0], value=args+2).

name: SE_ObjectFunctionExists
semantics: Returns 1 if the object with id objId (args[0].value is used as the id regardless of cell type) has a script method called name in its class or any parent class, else 0. Id resolution (ResolveObjectContext): id>=0 -> static class-record table lookup; id<0 -> script-created object hash keyed by (-id-1); unresolved id -> 0. Method search: name compared case-sensitively (binary search, byte compare) in each class's OWN method table (class+0x28 count / +0x2c rows), walking parent chain (class+0x14). Quirk: the loop only starts if the object's own class has the merged table pointer (+0x30) non-zero, and ends when the parent pointer is NULL. name not a string -> CellGetString NULL passed to the search (likely crash).
notes: ObjectHasMethod 0x0049f730, FindMethodByName 0x004b0740.

name: TI_AddTime
semantics: Returns a+b (32-bit wrapping add of args[0].value and args[1].value). No game state touched. Synchronous.
notes: Group TI dispatcher Script::TiDispatch 0x004b1300 (thunk 0x004b12d0), name table 0x00579f80 (index = (slot-0x579f80)/4).

name: SE_TableRandomKey
semantics: Returns a copy of the key of a uniformly chosen entry: n=TableCount(t); if n<=0 (or not a table) returns int 0. Else i=rand()*n/32768 (Math::RandScaled, CRT rand, 0..n-1) and returns the i-th (0-based) key in table iteration order (key cell copy: int or string). Returns int 0 if iteration yields nothing.
notes: RandScaled 0x004ee1c0 = (int64)n*rand()/0x8000 (truncating). Uses CRT rand() state (shared with TiScheduleDelay jitter etc.).

name: SE_ReadFile
semantics: Reads a whole file through the game virtual FS and returns its content as a heap string; returns int 0 on failure. Path splitting: find last '.'; if found name=path[0:dot] and ext string = "pck "+path[dot+1:] (e.g. "pck txt"); if no '.', name=whole path and ext="pck txt". Calls Archive::ResourceLoad(name, ext, flag) which resolves the name through the catalogue (.cat/.dat, unless flag) and loose files and returns the buffer; size is Archive::g_ResourceSize2. diskOnly=(argc>=2 && args[1].value!=0) disables the catalogue lookup; nulReplace=(argc>=3) low byte of args[2].value: if non-zero, every NUL byte in the buffer is replaced by that char before conversion. Result is built with SetCellStringDup(buf, size): a heap string of size bytes (embedded NULs would truncate a C string unless replaced). Buffer freed. Side effect: sets cfg flag 0x4000 in EngineConfig+0x108. Path argument that is not a string -> NULL passed to std::string ctor (crash).
notes: Uncertain: exact meaning of the "pck <ext>" variant (appears to be a packed/compressed alternative handled inside ResourceLoad/ResolveName; the plain file is the fallback). Emulator: read file from the game dir (or extracted catalogue) and return its bytes.

name: SE_QSortByInt
semantics: Sorts arr[start..end] (inclusive) by the 32-bit payload (value dword at cell+1, whatever the cell type) of keys[start..end]; the elements of arr are permuted (cells moved, not copied); keys is NOT modified. Executed only if: both args are arrays, start>=0, start<end, end<ArraySize(arr) and end<ArraySize(keys) (sizes read from the raw array header, lazy arrays with negative size fail the test); otherwise silent no-op. desc=(argc>=5 && args[4].value!=0): non-zero -> descending (comparator b.key-a.key), zero/absent -> ascending (a.key-b.key). Comparators are plain 32-bit subtraction (overflow wraps) fed to CRT qsort -> NOT stable, order of equal keys unspecified. Always returns int 0.
notes: ArraySortRangeByInt 0x004aa820; comparators 0x004ab160 (asc) and 0x004aa690 (desc). Arg order from dis: array=args[0], keyArray=args[1], start=args[2], end=args[3].

name: SE_IsString
semantics: Returns 1 if args[0] is a string cell (type 2 pool string or type 0xb heap string), else 0.

name: SE_FSize
semantics: File::GetSize: if diskOnly (argc>=2 && args[1].value!=0) is 0, first looks path up in the catalogue and returns its stored size; otherwise stat() of the normalized game path. Returns file size in bytes, -1 if missing (stat failed), -2 if it is a directory. Reads filesystem (side-effect free).
notes: Path normalization is File::NormalizeGamePath (relative to the game directory). Non-string path -> NULL (crash).

name: TI_WaitForInterrupt
semantics: Suspends the calling task until either the timeout expires or TI_Interrupt(key) is called with the same key. Delay node is queued with TiScheduleDelay: due = now(EngineConfig+0x718, game clock ms) + timeoutMs + jitter, jitter = rand()*J/32768 where J = (timeoutMs<0x1000 ? ((timeoutMs+(timeoutMs<0?15:0))>>4)+1 : 0x100) taken as 16-bit, and jitter=0 if J<1 (negative timeout). Node flagged 4 with interrupt key. Wake-up value: on timeout (TiTick: due-now<1 at a frame tick) the task resumes with int 0; when interrupted the task resumes with int (due - now) = remaining ms (may be <=0 only in odd cases). All waiters with a matching key are woken, in list (FIFO) order. Waiters with the same key set by other tasks are all released by one TI_Interrupt.
notes: Resume goes through the group completion callback (group record +4 = NativeCompletion) with the task id as argument. TiTick 0x004b0e00 runs once per main-loop iteration. TiScheduleDelayFlagged 0x004b0bd0, TiSignalInterrupt 0x004b0bf0. On node allocation failure the callback is called at once with (param,0).

name: SE_ArrayFind
semantics: Linear search from index start (start taken only if argc>2; negative/0 start -> 0) to size-1 for the first element equal to needle; returns its index or -1. Not an array -> size 0 -> -1; start>=size -> -1. Equality is Script::CellEquals(element, needle): int vs int by value; int vs double and double vs double numeric; string(2/0xb) vs string(2/0xb) byte-exact case-sensitive content compare; same-type arrays/tables/objects (8,9,0xa) by reference identity (pointer); any other mismatch of types falls to 'both falsy' test (CellIsTrue: 0, empty string pointer 0, null object, 0.0 are false): equal iff both are false. E.g. int 0 equals empty/zero double, int 5 vs string "5" is not equal. Same-type cells of other kinds (0,3,0xd,...) compare unequal. NULL element (out of range) is skipped.
notes: CellEquals 0x004a8a10. NOTE CellIsTrue returns true for string cells with non-zero offset/pointer, so an empty string is TRUE (it is a pointer).

name: SE_GetClass
semantics: Returns the class id (first dword of the class record) of an object. If args[0] is type 0xa (object ref): uses the object directly (returns 0 if its class pointer obj+8 is NULL). Otherwise args[0].value is treated as an object id and resolved with ResolveObjectContext (id>=0 static class records, id<0 dynamic objects); unresolved -> 0.
notes: Dispatcher default path returns int 0.

name: SE_ToInt
semantics: Type conversion with a trap: double (type 0xe) -> truncated toward zero (Crt::Ftol/fistp-style; out of range gives 0x80000000); string (type 2 or 0xb) -> atol() (leading whitespace, optional sign, decimal digits, stop at first non-digit, 0 if none, overflow wraps); EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDING int returns 0 (an int argument is NOT passed through).
notes: Verified in dis: only compares tags 0xe, 2, 0xb; other tags jump to the 'push int 0' stub.

name: SE_Distance3
semantics: Returns trunc(sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)) computed in floating point: each int is converted to float32 (precision loss above 2^24), squares/sum done in x87 extended precision then stored as float32, then FSQRT, then Crt::Ftol truncation toward zero. Takes the three args by value (args[0..2]).
notes: Math::VecLengthToInt 0x0049c880, SqrtF 0x00412440. For |components| < 2^24 result equals floor(sqrt(sum)) up to float32 rounding of the sum.

name: SE_StringXMLEscape
semantics: Returns s with the characters & < > " replaced by the entities & < > " (apostrophe is NOT escaped). Result is a new string. Non-string argument -> NULL -> crash.
notes: XmlEscapeString 0x004a6490 (two passes: length, then fill).

name: SE_RegFree
semantics: Releases the compiled regex with handle re (removes it from the VM regex map and frees the memory). Unknown/already freed handle: no effect. Always returns int 0.
notes: Map is Vm+0x15f4 (regexps).

name: SE_RegExec
semantics: Runs compiled regex re (from SE_RegComp) against s as an unanchored search (Henry Spencer regexec: tries each start position; ^ anchors at s start). Returns 1 if it matches anywhere, else 0. Unknown handle -> 0. Non-string s -> NULL -> 0. Exec also first rejects quickly using the regex's required literal if one was recorded. No capture results are exposed here (use the sibling Subst natives).
notes: Regex::Exec 0x004e6400; Henry Spencer v8 regexp variant (3-byte nodes, magic 0x9c). Syntax is the classic one: | ( ) * + ? . [ ] ^ $ and backslash escapes, no {n,m}, no non-greedy, case sensitive. Not fully verified against CompReg.

name: SE_RegComp
semantics: Compiles pattern with Regex::Compile (Henry Spencer regcomp) and returns a positive integer handle (auto id from Vm regex map +0x15f4, counter 1..0x7ffffffe), or int 0 if compilation fails (syntax error, NULL/non-string pattern, program too large >=0x7fff). Handles live until SE_RegFree.
notes: Counter start value (first handle presumably 1) not verified; HashMapAutoId 0x004efcc0 pre-increments.

name: SE_FPrintf
semantics: Formats fmt with the script printf (Script::FormatString, argc-2 extra cell args) and writes the text to the open file handle fh (from SE_FOpen) with fwrite. Returns the number of bytes written (=strlen of the formatted text; 0 for empty text) or 0 if fh is unknown, the file is not open for writing, or it came from the catalogue (read-only). Returns 0 and writes nothing if the temp buffer allocation fails. Format language: %[!N][flags -+ space # 0][width|*][.prec|.*][h|l|L] conv; conv d i u x X o (int cells; non-int cell prints 0), e E f F g G (double cells type 0xe only; other cell types print as 0.0), c (int cell), s (string cell, else the text <invalid>), a (any cell printed as debug text, arrays as [..]), %% literal. %!N picks explicit argument N (single digit) without consuming. Unknown conversion prints the % and the character. NULL fmt -> empty.
notes: Arg array passed to FormatString starts at args[2]. Write goes File::Write(f,1,len,buf) = fwrite(buf,1,len): return is item count = len.

name: SE_StringRChr
semantics: Index (byte offset) of the LAST occurrence of byte ch (low byte of args[1].value, CRT strrchr semantics) in s, or -1 if absent. ch==0 returns strlen(s). Non-string s (CellGetString NULL) -> -1.

name: SE_TimeString
semantics: strftime(buf[0x31], fmt, localtime64(t)) -> string. If argc==1 uses the current time (_time64), otherwise t=args[1].value taken as unsigned 32-bit zero-extended to 64-bit. Local time zone of the host. Output limited to 48 chars: if the formatted result does not fit the CRT call fails (returns 0) and the buffer content is whatever the CRT left (probably empty string); buf[0x31] is forced to 0. localtime64 failure (NULL) or non-string fmt -> CRT invalid-parameter handling (likely crash).
notes: Result via ResumeTaskWithString. Output depends on host clock/locale (C locale strftime). Emulator may substitute a fixed clock.

name: SE_GetRotMatrixFromAngles
semantics: Returns a 3x3 matrix as array of 3 row arrays of 3 ints (16.16 fixed point). Angles are 16-bit binary angles (value & 0xffff, 65536 = full turn): theta = (v&0xffff)*1.5258789e-05f*6.2831855f (float32 constants widened). With sa,ca = sin,cos(theta(a)); sb,cb = theta(b); sg,cg = theta(g) and K=65536.0 (each entry Ftol-truncated toward zero): row0 = [K*(sg*sb*sa + cg*ca), K*sg*cb, K*(cg*sa - sg*sb*ca)]; row1 = [K*(cg*sb*sa - sg*ca), K*cg*cb, -K*(sg*sa + cg*sb*ca)]; row2 = [-K*sa*cb, K*sb, K*ca*cb]. (Some intermediate products sg*sb and sb*cg are rounded to float32 once.)
notes: Math::AnglesToMatrix 0x004f0270 derived from x87 disassembly; matrix stored in 4-dword rows, handler packs the first 3 dwords of each row. Floating point order of operations may differ in the last ulp of the truncation; verify with a few sample angles if exactness at +-1 matters.

name: TI_SetTimeWarpFactor
semantics: Stores args[0].value unchanged into EngineConfig+0xcc (time-warp factor, 16.16 fixed point: 65536 = 1x) and returns int 1. Engine state side effect (game speed); TiTick later adapts EngineConfig+0xd0 (the effective multiplier) from the load.
notes: Entry of this case is hooked by x3-mod (seta_restore); original code: mov [cfg+0xcc],edx.

name: SE_XMLImport
semantics: Parses the XML TEXT passed in args[0] (not a path) with libxml2 xmlReadMemory (options 0x180 = no error/warning output; blanks are kept) and converts the root element to nested arrays. Returns int 0 if the text is NULL/not a string, fails to parse, or has no element root. Element -> array [tagName:string, attrs, child1, child2, ...]. attrs = int 0 when the element has no attributes, otherwise a table keyed by attribute-name string; each value is an INT (atol) if the attribute text is an optional leading '-' followed by 1+ decimal digits only, otherwise a string (an empty value or just "-" stays a string). Children in document order: element children -> nested arrays (recursive); text nodes (xml type 3, including whitespace-only text between tags and entity-decoded text) -> strings; comments, CDATA (type 4), PIs are skipped. Attribute table is a normal script table (insert via TableSet with growth), so its key iteration order follows the hash rules.
notes: XmlNodeToArray 0x004a7f60. Parse errors are silent. Array size = 2 + number of element/text children.

name: SE_Sqrt
semantics: Integer square root, floor(sqrt(n)), computed with the classic bit-by-bit algorithm (bit starts 0x40000000, signed compares). n==0 -> 0; negative n -> 0. Result for 0<=n<=2^31-1 is exactly floor(sqrt(n)).

name: SE_SetMaxOpCount
semantics: Sets Vm+0x1604 (maximum operation count per task slice, initial 10,000,000) to args[0].value and resets the running counter Vm+0x1608 to 0. Returns int 0. (Switch case 0x8e, the neighbouring native, shares this same code.)
notes: Purpose of the field is inferred from the name; the interpreter uses it as an instruction budget. Emulator can ignore or implement as budget.

name: SE_RandomLowNorm
semantics: Random with a bell-shaped distribution: sum n samples s_i = (2a>0 ? RandScaled(2a) : 0) (each uniform in [0,2a-1], CRT rand()*2a/32768), avg = sum / n (signed integer division truncating toward zero; sum=0 if n<=0). If avg < a then avg = 2a - avg - 1 (mirror). Returns avg - a. For a>0 the result is in [0, a-1]: the mean of n uniforms concentrates around a, the mirror step folds the lower half onto the upper half, so after subtracting a the result clusters near 0 (more so for larger n). n==0 raises a division-by-zero exception (crash). a<=0: avg=0, result = -a.
notes: Math::RandScaled 0x004ee1c0 = (int64)x*rand()/0x8000. Loop count n is read from args[1].value as signed; n<=0 skips the loop (but n==0 still divides).

name: SE_FOpen
semantics: Opens a file and returns a positive integer handle (auto id from Vm openFiles map +0x12d4, ids 1..0x7ffffffe), or int 0 on failure. diskOnly=(argc>2 && args[2].value!=0). File::OpenFromCatalogueOrDisk: unless diskOnly, the path is looked up in the game catalogue; a catalogue hit is opened from the archive file (fopen on the .dat with fseek to the entry offset) unless mode is exactly "w" or "wb" (then always a loose file); otherwise the normalized game path is fopen'ed with mode (standard CRT modes). Catalogue-backed handles are read-only (writes return 0). Sets cfg flag 0x4000 (EngineConfig+0x108). mode not a string -> NULL strlen (crash).
notes: Handles are closed with SE_FClose; leaked handles stay in the map. NormalizeGamePath resolves relative to the game directory.

name: SE_FClose
semantics: Closes and forgets the handle fh. Always returns int 0 (both for a valid handle and for an unknown one; unknown handle does nothing).

name: TI_GetTimeWarpFactor
semantics: Returns EngineConfig+0xcc (the 16.16 time-warp factor last set by TI_SetTimeWarpFactor / the game; 65536 = normal speed). Reads engine state.

name: SE_stricmp
semantics: If args[0] is not a string cell (type 2/0xb) returns -2; else if args[1] is not a string returns 2; otherwise returns CRT _stricmp(a,b): the difference lower(a[i])-lower(b[i]) at the first differing byte (ASCII A-Z folded, C locale), 0 if equal; NOT normalized to -1/0/1 (can be any int). Prefix: a shorter than b gives a negative number (0 - char).
notes: MSVC ___ascii_stricmp 0x00517a73: SUB EAX,ECX of lowered bytes. If the locale flag DAT_0057e27c is non-zero the locale-aware __stricmp_l is used instead (not normally the case).

name: SE_TableNumberedKey
semantics: Returns a copy of the key of the n-th entry (0-based) in iteration order, if t is a table with count>0 and 0<=n<count; otherwise int 0. Iteration order = ascending bucket index, chain order within a bucket (see SE_TableClone notes).
notes: O(n) walk with TableNextEntry.

name: SE_TableNew
semantics: Appends value (CopyCell) under a fresh automatic integer key and returns that key. Uses the per-table counter (table+0x10, initial 1): counter+=1 (wraps to 1 after 0x7ffffffe), skipping values that already exist as INT keys; the first key issued by a fresh table is therefore 2. Returns 0 if t is not a table or no free key was found after a full wrap. Insertion via TableInsertAndGrow (rehash when count>=4*buckets).
notes: TableAppendNextKey 0x004aaae0. Key 0 is never returned, so 0 means failure.

name: SE_TableData
semantics: Returns an array of the table's VALUES (copies) in iteration order, length = number of entries (empty array if t is not a table or is empty). Element i is the value of the i-th key as returned by SE_TableKeys.
notes: Iteration order as described for SE_TableClone.

name: SE_Sin
semantics: Fixed-point sine. angle is a 16-bit binary angle (a = angle & 0xffff, 65536 = full turn). Returns 16.16 value (-65536..65536) from the quarter-wave table T[k] (k=0..0x4000), T[k]=Ftol(sin(k*9.58738019107841e-05)*65536.0) (truncate toward zero; the angle step is float32(2*pi/65536) widened to double): a<=0x4000: T[a]; a<=0x8000: T[0x8000-a]; a<=0xC000: -T[a-0x8000]; else -T[0x10000-a]. So sin(0)=0, sin(0x4000)=65536, sin(0x8000)=0, sin(0xC000)=-65536.
notes: Table Math::g_SinCosTable 0x005b6998 is filled at startup by Math::BuildAsinTable 0x004f0110 (call from Init::EngineConfigInit). Emulator should rebuild the table with the same formula (x87 FSIN at extended precision; tiny last-digit differences are possible).

name: SE_Cos
semantics: Fixed-point cosine, same scale/table as SE_Sin: a = angle & 0xffff; a<=0x4000: T[0x4000-a]; a<=0x8000: -T[a-0x4000]; a<=0xC000: -T[0xC000-a]; else T[a-0xC000]. So cos(0)=65536, cos(0x4000)=0, cos(0x8000)=-65536, cos(0xC000)=0.
notes: See SE_Sin.

name: TI_WaitRandomForInterrupt
semantics: Like TI_WaitForInterrupt with timeout = baseMs + (randMs>0 ? RandScaled(randMs) : 0) (rand()*randMs/32768, 0..randMs-1), key=args[2].value. Then TiScheduleDelay adds its own extra jitter exactly as for TI_WaitForInterrupt. Resumes with int 0 on timeout, or the remaining ms when released by TI_Interrupt(key).
notes: See TI_WaitForInterrupt for scheduling details. Order of rand() calls: first the randMs roll, then the jitter roll inside TiScheduleDelay (only when jitter range>=1).

name: SE_WriteFile
semantics: Creates/overwrites a file with text (bytes of the C string) and returns the number of bytes written (strlen(text)); returns 0 if the file could not be opened or the write failed (note: empty text also returns 0 although the file is created empty). diskOnly=(argc>2 && args[2].value!=0), gzip=(argc>3 ? args[3].value : 0). gzip==0: File::OpenFromCatalogueOrDisk(path,"wb",diskOnly) (always a loose file for mode wb); gzip!=0: gzopen(normalized path,"wb") and the data are gz-compressed. Single fwrite/gzwrite of the whole string, then closes. Side effect: writes to disk; sets cfg flag 0x4000.
notes: Success test is File::Write(...)==1 where it is called as fwrite(buf,len,1). Non-string text -> NULL (crash).
